## Best of Ecuador: an 11-day tour with guaranteed departures and the Galápagos

The [Best of Ecuador: Guaranteed Departures tour](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) combines **11 days and 10 nights** of travel through mainland Ecuador and the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The first section covers colonial cities, crater lakes, waterfalls, and highland nature reserves. The final four days are devoted to the archipelago, with giant tortoises, lava fields, and marine excursions.

We offer this itinerary for a small group of **up to 16 travelers**. A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the mainland portion, while the main Galápagos excursions are led in English. Some airport transfers have drivers who speak other languages; this detail is particularly important when choosing a group tour.

## How the route is organized

| Days | Main regions |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Quito and the equator line |
| 3–4 | Quilotoa, Baños, Riobamba |
| 5–7 | Chimborazo, Ingapirca, Cuenca, Cajas |
| 8–11 | Galápagos: Santa Cruz, Bartolomé, marine islands |

The itinerary combines the Andes and the Pacific archipelago in one trip. There are many moves, however: hotels change, and some days involve lengthy drives and early starts.

## First days: Quito, the equator, and Quilotoa

After arriving in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), the group checks in at Hotel Finlandia 4*, with dinner alongside the guide scheduled for the evening. The following day explores the historic center, Baroque architecture, and two equator-related sites: Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum.

On day three, the route passes a flower plantation before reaching [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) inside a volcanic crater and then [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). The rose plantation is **closed to visitors on weekends and public holidays**. Descending to the lake and climbing back, mule rides, and kayaking depend on conditions and may involve extra payment.

Day four focuses on Baños and its waterfalls. The itinerary lists Agoyán, Manto de la Novia, and Pailón del Diablo, followed by a transfer to Riobamba.

## Chimborazo, Ingapirca, and Cuenca

Day five includes [Chimborazo Reserve](/ecuador/place/chimborazo-reserve/), with high-altitude landscapes and Andean camelids, and the archaeological site of [Ingapirca](/ecuador/place/ingapirca/). A packed lunch is planned for this long excursion day. The source program notes a restriction on Ingapirca's opening arrangements: if the ruins are closed, only an exterior viewing may be possible. Check actual opening rules before the trip.

The following day in [Cuenca](/ecuador/place/cuenca/) is devoted to its historic center, cathedrals, museums, and architecture. On day seven, travelers pass through [Cajas National Park](/ecuador/place/cajas-national-park/), known for numerous mountain lakes, and visit a cocoa hacienda where lunch is included. The group then continues to Guayaquil.

## The final four days: the Galápagos Islands

On day eight, travelers fly from [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/) to Baltra Airport and transfer to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The island program includes giant tortoises, lava tunnels, and accommodation in Puerto Ayora.

Day nine is devoted to [Bartolomé Island](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/): a boat crossing, an ascent to a panoramic viewpoint, volcanic terrain, and a marine excursion. On day ten there are **two alternative routes**: North Seymour with Bachas Beaches **or** South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The actual option is confirmed after booking; visiting every listed island in one day is not promised.

Day eleven includes breakfast, a transfer to Baltra Airport, and a flight back to Quito or Guayaquil, where the international journey continues.

## What to consider when paying

The group tour price starts **from $3995**. It includes accommodation in the specified hotels, meals scheduled by day, excursions and ground transfers, guides in the stated formats, and entrance tickets to main mainland attractions.

However, **the Galápagos involve separate mandatory expenses**, explicitly listed in the tour terms: the Guayaquil–islands–Quito/Guayaquil flights ($575 per person), national park admission ($200 per person), and the INGALA transit card ($20 per person). The published terms also mention a discount on park admission for children under 12. These figures are the program's stated conditions; actual charges and payment rules must be checked against current regulations before departure. International flights and insurance are also paid separately.

## Dates and the group format

The tour lists departures **for 2026**, including October and November. This is the historical schedule for a particular season: available seats or new departures cannot be inferred from it automatically. Booking requires a confirmed group date, since the island portion must be arranged around it.

The advantage of a group itinerary is an organized sequence of several regions. At the same time, the group format sets the route and guiding languages, and travelers do not freely choose between the two island alternatives.

If you want only mainland Ecuador and a more relaxed stay in one city, compare the [5-day private tour from Quito](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-private-tour-5-days/). For a deeper Amazon experience, consider the [9-day M/V Anaconda program](/ecuador/tour/luxury-mainland-ecuador-9-days/). The full selection is in our [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about guaranteed departures

### Does the tour name guarantee a departure on any chosen date?

No. Specific departure dates for 2026 are published; a place in the group and departures in another season require separate confirmation.

### Are all Galápagos island excursions included on a single trip?

No. Day ten offers **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour and Bachas or South Plaza and Cape Carrión.

### What additional expenses apply in the Galápagos?

The island flights, national park entrance, and INGALA transit card are charged separately under the tour terms. International flights are also excluded.

### Which languages are used on excursions?

The primary mainland guiding is in Russian, while Galápagos excursions are in English. The first and final transfers have separate language conditions stated in the program.

## All of Ecuador and the Galápagos in 8 days: how the journey works

The [Complete Ecuador and Galápagos Islands tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-galapagos-islands/) combines **8 days and 7 nights**, two strikingly different regions of the country, and several natural environments. The first four days are on the mainland: Quito, Mindo cloud forest, and Quilotoa crater lake. Next come the flight to the Galápagos, Santa Cruz Island, a marine outing to Bartolomé, and one of two options for a second day at sea.

We offer this route to travelers interested in historic cities, forest ecosystems, volcanic landscapes, and the archipelago's animals. The key choice is less about the number of excursions than **the balance between mainland and island stages**: each receives four calendar days, including transfers.

## Mainland days: from Quito to cloud forest

The first stop is [Quito and the Cotopaxi region](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). Arrival includes a welcome and transfer to the hotel, with the rest of the day free. The following day introduces the historic center, colonial architecture, old churches, and squares. The route then visits the Mitad del Mundo complex and Intiñan Museum.

The capital stands at around **2,850 meters** above sea level. Even without a sporting ascent, it is sensible to consider the elevation after a flight. A low-exertion evening gives travelers time to adjust before the excursion days.

Day three takes the group to [Mindo](/ecuador/place/mindo/). Cloud forest, orchids, butterflies, and birds replace the stone streets. The itinerary includes a butterfly farm, a cable car above the vegetation, a nature walk, and a chocolate tour. This provides an introduction to a completely different Ecuadorian environment before reaching the archipelago.

Day four leads to [Quilotoa Lagoon](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/). On the way, the group visits a Tigua workshop known for local painting and then reaches the crater lake. Walking down to the shore is on the program; returning by mule and kayaking are listed as possible activities, whose terms must be distinguished from the main excursion. Unlike the [9-day Active Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/), there is no promised six-hour circuit around the caldera.

## How the Galápagos stage begins

On day five, the group flies from the mainland to Baltra Airport. After meeting the guide, travelers cross Itabaca Channel and drive through [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) toward Puerto Ayora. This is more than a transfer to the hotel: the route includes the island highlands, where giant Galápagos tortoises can be seen in their natural habitat.

On Santa Cruz, dry coastal areas contrast with wetter highland landscapes. Animal habitats change with the vegetation and elevation. For a nature visit, bring suitable walking shoes, a hat, and sun protection.

Day six is a marine excursion to [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/). The yacht crossing takes around **2 hours**. After landing, there is an ascent of approximately half an hour along a volcanic slope to a viewpoint famous for views of Pinnacle Rock and neighboring islands. Beach time and snorkeling follow, with lunch served on board.

The day combines travel by boat, a short hike, and time in the water. Those prone to seasickness should prepare beforehand. Snorkeling is stated as part of the itinerary, but sea conditions and wildlife sightings depend on nature and the decisions of the guides.

## North Seymour or South Plaza: why are there two options?

Day seven offers a sea excursion to **one of two islands**, with the option confirmed after booking. [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) is particularly known for seabirds, including blue-footed boobies and frigatebirds. South Plaza features land iguanas, sea lion colonies, and distinctive coastal vegetation. If South Plaza is chosen, the program also includes Cape Carrión and snorkeling.

Do not expect to visit **both** islands in a day: the itinerary offers alternatives. Before booking, discuss the confirmed option with Ada Tours, along with sea conditions and your own interests, whether seabirds, land animals, or swimming.

Visits to protected sites follow authorized national park routes. Keeping a distance from animals and not feeding them are essential. Encounters with specific species or individuals cannot be guaranteed.

## Guiding and flights: points to check

On the mainland, the tour terms provide **private transfers and excursions**, with a Russian-speaking guide or driver-guide. On the Galápagos, the format changes: transfers and excursions are **shared group activities** led by an English-speaking guide. The final airport transfer has a Spanish-speaking escort. This distinction matters especially to those who want explanations in Russian throughout the trip.

Accommodation, specified meals, excursion transfers, and mainland attraction tickets are included. On the islands, early starts, boat crossings, and organized walks occupy much of the day, with free evenings after returning to Puerto Ayora.

The trip price starts **from 3439 USD**. Separately listed expenses include international flights, insurance, tips, personal spending, **Quito–Galápagos–Quito or Guayaquil flights (515 USD per person)**, **Galápagos National Park admission (200 USD per person)**, and **the Galápagos transit card (20 USD per person)**. These last three costs are significant when comparing another program that already includes some documentation fees. Government charges may differ by visitor category.

## Comparing similar itineraries

| Itinerary | Main difference |
|---|---|
| 8 days: Ecuador and Galápagos | Mindo, Quilotoa, two marine days |
| 9 days: Active Ecuador | Trekking, canyoning, rafting |
| 11 days: New Year | Holiday departure and a longer Andean route |

[Active Ecuador](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) is intended for travelers who want to walk mountain trails and participate in water activities. The [New Year Ecuador and Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) covers more mainland places and is tied to **December 30, 2026–January 9, 2027**. The 8-day itinerary is more compact but allows less time for independent stops outside the established route.

Choose according to your main goal. For wildlife observation, the island stage adds dedicated days beyond what an Andes-only trip offers. If you prioritize relaxed travel without boat crossings, compare other [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) or [the Galápagos as a destination](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) before fixing your dates.

## Frequently asked questions about Ecuador and the Galápagos

### How long is the mainland stage?

The first **4 days** take place on the mainland: Quito, Mindo, and Quilotoa. The flight to the Galápagos is scheduled **on day five**.

### Do you need to speak English?

The mainland stage has a Russian-speaking guide or driver-guide. Galápagos excursions are led in English, which is worth considering when choosing the trip.

### Are park admission and the transit card included?

No. For this tour, both are listed as separate expenses together with the flights to the islands. The inclusions may differ in another itinerary.

### Will you see every animal mentioned?

The Galápagos offer opportunities to observe tortoises, seabirds, iguanas, and marine animals in their habitat. Individual encounters depend on the itinerary, weather, and wild animals' behavior, so no complete species list can be guaranteed.

## New Year in Ecuador 2026/2027: Andes, Quito, and Galápagos in 11 days

The [Ecuador New Year tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) is scheduled **from December 30, 2026, to January 9, 2027**. This is a group itinerary of **11 days and 10 nights**, with **up to 15 participants**. New Year is celebrated in Quito, after which the route continues through the Andean highlands, Baños, Chimborazo, Cuenca, and Guayaquil to the Galápagos Islands.

Unlike a general sightseeing trip, this departure follows a fixed calendar: the festive evening is in the capital and the island stage concludes the journey. It suits travelers who want to explore several of Ecuador's natural environments during one New Year holiday and are comfortable changing cities and hotels frequently.

## Where is New Year celebrated?

**December 30** is the arrival day in Quito, followed by hotel check-in. On **December 31**, the group explores the historic capital and the equator line; a festive hotel dinner with music and dancing is scheduled for the evening. The sequence is important: participants do not need to seek a separate New Year event in another city and then catch up with the group in the Andes.

[Quito and the Cotopaxi region](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) are at high elevation. Quito stands approximately 2,800–2,850 meters above sea level, so it is best to take things slowly after a long flight. Even a non-mountaineering sightseeing day can feel unusual to travelers arriving from lowlands.

From **January 1**, the mainland journey involves frequent transfers. The route passes Tigua workshops and [Quilotoa crater lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) before reaching Baños. The following day includes waterfalls and the road to Riobamba; next come the [Chimborazo](/ecuador/place/chimborazo-reserve/) region, the Ingapirca archaeological complex, and Cuenca.

## From the Andes to the coast: how the scenery changes

The itinerary combines geography and culture: Quito and Cuenca are historic cities, Quilotoa is a volcanic caldera, while Baños features humid gorges and waterfalls. Drives across the highlands call for clothing suitable for cool, windy weather. In Guayaquil and on the islands, lighter clothes are needed for warmer conditions.

**January 5** includes cocoa-related activities after the Cajas National Park area and a transfer to Guayaquil. **January 6**, the group flies to the Galápagos. This schedule brings the Andes and islands together but leaves few days without travel. If long stays in one place matter more, compare other [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/).

In [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), the tour includes visits to waterfalls. Optional activities are also listed: kayaking and a mule ride at Quilotoa cost extra, and a canopy activity over the Pastaza Canyon is a separate service. They should not be treated as mandatory parts of the main itinerary.

## Four days in the Galápagos

The island stage runs from **January 6 to 9, 2027**. After landing at Baltra, travelers reach [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and visit its highlands to observe giant tortoises. A marine excursion then visits [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/), with volcanic landscapes, a viewpoint, and snorkeling according to the program.

On **January 8**, there is **one of two alternatives**: [North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) with Bachas Beach, **or** South Plaza with Cape Carrión. These are alternative marine routes, not a promise to see every island. The selected option is confirmed after booking.

Protected-area rules apply on the islands: visitor sites are reached on authorized routes and wildlife observation requires a safe distance. Penguins, iguanas, sea lions, and birds are important reasons to visit the Galápagos, but wild animals move freely, so no encounter with every species can be guaranteed. Read more in the [Galápagos Islands guide](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

## Trip prices and expenses paid separately

We offer per-person prices depending on room occupancy:

| Accommodation | Price |
|---|---:|
| TPL, triple | 4250 USD |
| DBL, double | 4325 USD |
| SGL, single | 4970 USD |

The tour includes group transfers and excursions, accommodation in the named or equivalent hotels, specified meals, excursion admission tickets, and **the Galápagos transit card**. A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the mainland stage, with an English-speaking driver on the first transfer; Galápagos excursions have an English-speaking guide, and the final transfer has a Spanish-speaking escort.

**Expenses listed separately** include international flights, medical and travel insurance, personal expenses, and tips. The domestic **Guayaquil–Galápagos–Quito or Guayaquil flight** is priced at **515 USD per person** and is not part of the tour price. Galápagos National Park admission is also separate: **200 USD per person** is stated in the program, with a discount for children under 12. The applicable government charge depends on visitor category, so confirm the current fee before paying.

When choosing room occupancy, compare the full budget: the tour price, international flights, separate island flight, park admission, and insurance. The table alone does not include every expense.

## Preparing for the itinerary

At the end of December and beginning of January, travelers encounter different weather and types of transportation: walks in high-altitude cities, drives through the Andes, a flight to the archipelago, and marine excursions. It helps to pack clothes for cool elevations, lighter garments for the coast, and protection against sun and water on island days.

Pay particular attention to arriving **by December 30**. The festive evening and later itinerary follow fixed dates, not a free choice of departure. Entry requirements, transit documents, and passport validity must be checked for each participant's nationality and actual flights before buying tickets. Ada Tours can help coordinate these matters, but authorized authorities make the final entry decisions.

If New Year celebrations are not essential, compare the [8-day Complete Ecuador and Galápagos itinerary](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-galapagos-islands/). It is shorter, focuses on Quito, Mindo, Quilotoa, and the islands, and uses a different transfer schedule.

## Frequently asked questions about New Year in Ecuador

### When does the New Year tour start and finish?

The departure is scheduled **December 30, 2026–January 9, 2027**, totaling 11 days and 10 nights. New Year is celebrated in Quito.

### Can you visit North Seymour and South Plaza on the same day?

The published program offers an alternative on January 8: **North Seymour or South Plaza**. The actual island is confirmed after booking.

### Is the Galápagos flight included in the price?

No. It is priced separately, as is Galápagos National Park admission. The islands' transit card, however, is included.

### Which guiding languages are offered?

The mainland stage includes a Russian-speaking guide, with a separate exception for the first transfer. Galápagos excursions are conducted in English, with a Spanish-speaking escort on the final transfer.

## Active Ecuador and Galápagos tour for 17 days: how demanding is it?

Travelers choose this route for **physical activity and demanding nature experiences**, not merely sightseeing. The program includes the cable car above Quito, [Mindo](/ecuador/place/mindo/) cloud forest, a five-day mountain trekking stage, rafting on the [Quijos River](/ecuador/place/quijos-river/), [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) waterfalls, Chimborazo Reserve, and finally the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

The trip lasts **17 days and 16 nights**. Nearly two weeks are spent on the mainland, with the islands bringing the journey to a close. It differs substantially from the [14-day Mashpi nature tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/), which focuses more on staying at a forest lodge and observing nature. Here, the main experiences are physically active.

## Five mountain days: Pasochoa, Rumiñahui, Ilinizas, Quilotoa, and Chimborazo

After visiting [Quito and Cotopaxi](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), the route heads into the mountains. Part of the program covers Pasochoa and Rumiñahui, followed by Ilinizas Reserve and North Iliniza. Another day is dedicated to trekking around [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/), with the [Chimborazo](/ecuador/place/chimborazo-volcano/) area as the next high-altitude stage.

According to the itinerary, several days are spent at elevations of around **4,000–5,000 meters**. Even fit travelers may feel the effects of thinner air. Fitness helps with walking but does not by itself protect against altitude sickness. Consider previous high-altitude experience, the rate of ascent, health, and acclimatization before departure.

Preparation calls for broken-in hiking boots, warm layers, ultraviolet and rain protection. **Personal trekking equipment is not included** in the base price. Agree on technical gear and acceptable conditions for each section before departure; no summit can be promised in all weather.

## Quijos rafting and the contrast with Baños waterfalls

On day nine, the itinerary includes **rafting on the Quijos River**, graded IV–IV+. This is technically demanding whitewater. Before taking part, consider actual water levels, experience, medical conditions, a professional guide's instructions, and individual restrictions. For anyone lacking appropriate preparation, this stage may determine whether the entire trip is suitable.

The journey then continues toward [Papallacta](/ecuador/place/papallacta/) and [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). The experience changes: after the highlands and rafting, the Pastaza Valley, waterfalls, and nature stops come to the fore. This stage reveals another part of Ecuador, but the effort already expended remains important. On successive active days, recovery and energy reserves matter as much as transport arrangements.

## Cuenca, Cajas, and the transition to ocean islands

The second part of the mainland itinerary includes Riobamba, Ingapirca, [Cuenca](/ecuador/place/cuenca/), and [Cajas National Park](/ecuador/place/cajas-national-park/). Travelers encounter Andean landscapes and historic monuments before reaching Guayaquil.

This stage takes the group from the central Andes toward the Pacific coast, rather than introducing another difficult climb. The flight to the archipelago begins from here. Pack warm clothing and boots for highland trails separately from lightweight clothes suitable for warmer, humid weather and boat excursions.

## The Galápagos: why the finale is different from the mainland

**Day fourteen** includes a flight through Baltra to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The island stage then includes a boat excursion to [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) and an alternative day: **North Seymour or South Plaza**. The final day is devoted to leaving the islands.

Activities are different here: boarding boats, walking on authorized trails, and observing animals and birds. No itinerary guarantees sightings of every well-known species. In the national park, visitors must keep their distance from wildlife, stay on marked paths, and follow local guides' instructions.

The island finale is particularly welcome after the Andes, but it is not an extended beach holiday. Travelers primarily interested in exploring more islands on a cruise should compare the [18-day yacht journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/).

## Services and separately paid expenses

The mainland stage includes **private transfers and excursions**, apart from group rafting. Galápagos excursions and transfers are shared. An English-speaking guide accompanies the main program, and the final island hotel-to-airport transfer has a Spanish-speaking escort.

The tour costs **$7265**. It includes hotels, meals, and admission tickets according to the confirmed itinerary, together with the described transfers and excursions. International flights, the Galápagos flight, insurance, trekking equipment, government island fees, tips, and personal expenses are listed separately.

When comparing this product with a standard sightseeing [Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/), first assess your readiness for **five mountain days and rafting**, then compare prices and numbers of attractions.

## Frequently asked questions about the active tour

### Is it suitable for someone without mountain hiking experience?

The itinerary includes multi-day high-altitude treks and IV–IV+ rafting. Assess physical and technical preparedness, altitude experience, and health restrictions before booking. Being comfortable with ordinary walks is not sufficient preparation.

### Does excellent fitness prevent altitude sickness?

No. Risk also depends on elevation, ascent speed, and individual adaptation. Even fit travelers need sensible acclimatization.

### Is the Galápagos stage private too?

No. Galápagos excursions are shared group activities, although many mainland excursions and transfers are private.

### Does the program include both North Seymour and South Plaza?

No. Day sixteen provides an alternative marine itinerary to one of these islands. Visiting both is not guaranteed.

## Ecuador, Galápagos, and humpback whales: August 11–21, 2027 itinerary

This 11-day journey has two distinct wildlife themes: the island animals of the Galápagos and the seasonal appearance of humpback whales off Ecuador's Pacific coast. Between them lies an Andean stage with historic Quito, high-altitude Quilotoa Lagoon, and the waterfalls of Baños.

**Tour dates: August 11–21, 2027; 11 days and 10 nights.** This is a particular Ada Tours itinerary with fixed dates, accommodation, and conditions. Do not confuse it with other [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) programs, which may cover different islands and omit whale watching.

## August 11–14: the capital, volcanic lake, and Baños

The trip begins in [Quito and the Cotopaxi region](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). After arrival, a hotel transfer is arranged; the following day brings sightseeing in the city and a visit to the equator line. Quito's historic center is known for colonial squares and churches and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

On August 13, the route passes through the Cotopaxi Valley, a rose plantation, and Tigua village before reaching [Quilotoa crater lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/). Along the way, travelers see changes in highland settlements and vegetation. Optional activities by the lake must be checked separately: the main itinerary does not automatically include every hiking or water-based option.

Guests then reach [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), a town amid green Andean slopes known for waterfalls and nature activities. The August 14 program follows the Route of the Waterfalls before returning to Quito.

## August 15–17: the Galápagos and an alternative island excursion

On August 15, the group flies to the archipelago. From Baltra Airport, travelers reach [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and Puerto Ayora. A visit to the island's interior includes giant tortoises and lava tunnels.

August 16 is dedicated to [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/). The island is known for its lava landscapes, distinctive shore, and lookout point over the ocean and island formations. This marine excursion differs from an ordinary trip on Santa Cruz, so it involves an early departure and travel time.

**On August 17, travelers visit one of two alternatives**, not both:

| Option | Places visited |
|---|---|
| [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) | The island and Bachas Beaches |
| [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) | The island and Cape Carrión |

## August 18–21: the coast and humpback whales

On August 18, the route continues through [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/) to [Punta Centinela](/ecuador/place/punta-centinela/), with **3 nights at Decameron Punta Centinela**. After the mainland and island activities, there is time to rest by the ocean. The accommodation is offered on an all-inclusive basis.

August 19 is a free day at the coast. **August 20** is reserved for a boat outing to watch humpback whales. This excursion distinguishes the program from other Ecuador journeys. Whale-watching trips depart from the hotel with specialists aboard the boat, without a separate general tour guide.

Humpback whales usually visit Ecuador's Pacific coast from June through September, with August being a principal observation period. However, **sightings of wild whales can never be guaranteed**, nor can particular behavior such as tail displays, breaching, or distance from the boat. Wind and sea conditions also affect whether the outing can take place.

On August 21, travelers transfer to Guayaquil for their return flight.
